summary: Michihiko Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He served there as an assistant (attested 1978–1980) and professor (~1996–2016), and held posts at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute and Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies.

Michihiko Yajima, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, pursued graduate studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 1981). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1992) and as professor at Tsurumi Women's University (attested 2003).

Michihiro Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar. His career includes posts as a lecturer at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), as well as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005).

Michiko Yusa is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed her doctoral studies under Raimon Panikkar (~1978–1983) and served as a professor in the Department of Foreign Languages at Western Washington University (~1983–2021).
Michio Kamikawa is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ritsumeikan University and held an attested post at Aichi Prefectural University in 2016.

Michio Yano is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi, earning a doctorate in 1996, and at Brown University under David Pingree. He served as a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from 1973 to 2015.

Michitaro Tanaka was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University under Hidenaka Tanaka (~1923–1926) and later taught Takeshi Umehara. His career included posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1947–1950) and Ryukoku University.

Michitoshi Baraida is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He held posts at Otani University, Toho Gakuin, Toho Kenkyukai, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Michiya Ito was a graduate student at Tohoku University (attested 1986–1990) and later held an attested post there between 2001 and 2004.

Michiyo Hoshi is a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. She has held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa as a collaborative researcher and at Toyo Bunko as a researcher (attested 2003).
Midori Nishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and later served there as a researcher (attested 2010–2015).

Migmar Tsering was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He served as head of Sakya College (attested 1991–2003) and held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences.

Mihai Șora was a philosopher who studied under Mircea Eliade at the University of Bucharest (~1934–1938), then at the University of Paris (~1938–1945) and CNRS (~1945–1948). He held a post at the State Publishing House for Literature and Arts (~1961–1969).

Mikaël Bauer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Kanazawa University under Paul Hoornaert and Noritoshi Aramaki, and earned a PhD at Harvard under Ryuichi Abe; he is an Associate Professor of Japanese Religions at McGill University.

Mikel Burley is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Essex under Jay M. Bernstein, earned a PhD at Bristol supervised by John Peacock, and became an Associate Professor of Religion and Philosophy at the University of Leeds.
Miki Ujiie is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She undertook research study at Tribhuvan University and held an attested post as a lecturer at Koyasan University in 1970.
Mikio Otsuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. In 2007, he held attested posts as a professor at Hanazono University and as a research fellow at Manpuku-ji.

Mikisaburo Mori was a philosophy and sinology scholar who studied at Kyoto University and earned a doctorate from Osaka University. He held posts at Kyoto University, the Academy of Oriental Culture, Osaka High School, Osaka University (professor 1966–1973), and Bukkyo University.

Milman Parry was a linguistics scholar who studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Paris, where he was supervised by Antoine Meillet. He later held an academic post at Harvard University from ~1929 until 1935.

Milton Singer was a scholar of Indology. He studied at the University of Texas at Austin (~1930–1936) and the University of Chicago (~1936–1940), where he subsequently held a faculty post from ~1940 to 1979.
